title: 9 Best Metaview alternatives by tool type
summary: Metaview covers interview notes and basic sourcing, but many teams need more. Compare 9 alternatives across sourcing, ATS, and interview intelligence.
body_markdown:
Recruitment teams use Metaview to generate interview transcripts and summaries and, with its new sourcing feature, to find candidates. But interview documentation and basic sourcing cover only part of recruiting work, and many teams have broader needs: CRM, ATS, outreach, and deeper sourcing than Metaview offers.


Teams that need broader coverage will need to look for other tools, either by choosing an all-in-one platform or integrating a curated stack of apps that support distinct parts of the hiring process.


Here, discover the nine best Metaview alternatives organized by the job to be done.


##


**Why teams look for Metaview alternatives**


Metaview started as an interview intelligence tool and has since expanded into other features like AI-assisted sourcing, application reviews, and reporting. The most developed part of the platform is note-taking, which it was originally built to perform, but its agentic workflows aren’t as robust as those integral to other top tools on the market.


Users move from Metaview for the following reasons.


-


**Sourcing depth:** Metaview’s sourcing agent is relatively new, and teams needing to find the right candidates fast may prefer to rely on a purpose-built, proven sourcing tool.


-


**À la carte cost adds up:** Metaview prices each agent (notes, sourcing, reviews, etc.) separately, so costs quickly add up. Teams needing multiple agents might instead prefer to build a stack of focused tools that cover distinct parts of the recruiting process well.


-


**Specific needs:** Even if a team doesn’t need additional functionality, they may phase out of Metaview because they need more customization, a different type of data export, or other practical requirements. Here, the team would look for a tool that replaces Metaview for interview intelligence—not necessarily one that can do other functions.


###


**How to choose the right tool category**


To figure out what category of tool you need, assess where your processes are weakest. This pain point indicates a gap your new tool can fill.


-


If you can’t find enough qualified candidates, you need a sourcing tool.


-


If your interview intelligence is too thin or you need to be able to interview in languages or formats that Metaview doesn’t support, you’ll be looking for a more robust interview tool.


-


If you don’t have single source of truth for your hiring information, you likely need an ATS (for tracking application progress) or a CRM (for coordinating tasks and sharing documentation internally).


##


**The 9 best Metaview alternatives**


###


**Sourcing**


1.


#### [Juicebox](https://juicebox.ai/)


If your team is struggling to source the required volume of high-quality candidates, rather than manage screening and interviews, adding a sourcing layer like Juicebox is the best way to improve your pipeline and efficiency. Juicebox enables you to search in plain language over 800 million profiles with verified contact details, while providing up-to-date talent intelligence on key data points like compensation by geography or talent flow.


Juicebox’s autonomous agents also run outreach (with a recruiter in the loop). The agents can initiate communication with candidates and also recommend the next messages to send so that conversations never drop off.


Juicebox has a built-in recruiting CRM and also integrates with interviewing tools and over 50 ATSs, fitting seamlessly into any tool stack.


**Best for:** Any type or size of recruiting team that needs more sourcing depth and wants plain-language search and AI agents to run outreach.


###


**Recruiting-focused interview intelligence**


1.


#### [BrightHire](https://brighthire.com/)


BrightHire can automate first-round interviews, and provides recording, transcription and AI-generated notes of the interviews your team conducts themselves. After interviews, BrightHire also provides candidate summaries and topic coverage to support decision-making, which can be useful for providing feedback to interview candidates.


**Best for:** Teams who want to fully automate their first-round screening, and still need solid interview intelligence.


1.


#### [Screenloop](https://www.screenloop.com/)


Screenloop provides interview transcription and summaries, as well as more detailed scoring to rank candidates. The platform uses AI to complete an interview scorecard, significantly reducing the interviewer's workload. In comparison to BrightHire, Screenloop's deeper ranking power is also integrated into a wider ATS.


Screenloop itself acts as an ATS, and BrightHire offers two-way integration with a wide range of the most commonly used systems, importing candidate and interview details, and writing back notes and scorecards.


**Best for** : Teams looking for the most detailed candidate scoring or for those looking to buy or replace their ATS.


###


**General meeting and async screening**


1.


#### [Fireflies](https://fireflies.ai/)


Fireflies is an AI meeting assistant that records, transcribes, and summarizes video meetings, including interviews, across Zoom, Google Meet, Teams, and Webex. It pulls out action items and lets you search across every transcript in plain language, and its free plan works with any account (including a free Zoom account).


**Best for:** Budget-conscious teams that want cross-platform AI transcription for interviews and general meetings alike, not a recruiting-specific tool.


1.


#### [Zoom AI Companion](https://www.zoom.com/)


Zoom’s built-in AI records, transcribes, and summarizes meetings and pulls action items, at no extra cost on any paid Zoom plan. It's a fine starting point if you already run interviews on Zoom, but it only covers Zoom calls and doesn't integrate with your ATS or recruiting stack. (Zoom retired the "AI Companion" name in mid-2026 and folded the features into Zoom Workplace, so it may appear under that name.)


**Best for:** Teams already on a paid Zoom plan that just need basic interview transcripts and summaries and don't want to add another tool.


1.


#### [Hireflix](https://hireflix.com/)


Hireflix is one-way (asynchronous) video interview software: you record your questions once, candidates answer on their own time, and your team reviews and rates the responses whenever it suits them, no scheduling required. It integrates with your ATS and is purpose-built for this single job.


**Best for:** Teams screening high volumes early in the funnel that want to replace repetitive first-round scheduling with async video. Note it's a screening add-on, not an ATS or interview-intelligence tool.


###


**ATS-native options**


1.


#### [Ashby](https://www.ashbyhq.com/)


Ashby's interview notetaker is closely integrated within the ATS and has the potential for more advanced analytics as its conversation intelligence enables it to understand context and nuanced meaning in an interview, and not just the words themselves. It can also undertake candidate screening, making it a great option if you're dealing with high-volume hiring.


**Best for:** Teams that want interview intelligence built directly into their ATS, and a strong fit for high-volume hiring given its first-round screening.


1.


#### [Greenhouse](https://www.greenhouse.com/)


Greenhouse's ATS has an AI notetaker integrated within it that generates structured notes and can produce interview summaries mapped to specific scorecard questions.


Greenhouse is the most expensive option but is particularly good if your team wants to retain a human-first approach to its hiring, and ensure rigorous compliance. This is because Greenhouse is focused on highly structured processes and has strict data governance built-in.


**Best for:** Teams that want a human-first, highly structured hiring process with rigorous compliance and data governance, and are willing to pay a premium for it.


1.


#### [Employ](https://www.employinc.com/)


Employ is the parent company behind several ATS platforms, including JazzHR, Lever, and Jobvite, and it offers an AI interview companion alongside them. The companion handles the core interview-intelligence basics: recording, transcription, structured notes, and some analysis of each interview, so evaluations are captured consistently rather than typed from memory. Because it sits beside Employ's own ATS products, teams already on one of those systems can add interview intelligence without introducing a separate vendor or a new integration to maintain.


**Best for:** Teams already using one of Employ's ATS platforms, or those wanting a simpler starting point.


##


**Metaview alternatives by use case**


Here are a few of the most common use cases behind a shift from Metaview.


-


**If you’re hiring at high volume and overwhelmed with screening:** Hireflix is a good choice, as it facilitates one-way, asynchronous interviews for first-round screening at scale.


-


**If you want to stick with an integrated, ATS-native workflow:** Ashby is the best option, with a high-quality interview notetaker and analysis integrated into its platform.


-


**If you want to improve interview quality:** BrightHire is a solid option, with integrated guidance, coaching, and real-time support for interviewers.


-


**If you need to boost your sourcing** : Juicebox strengthens your pipeline with plain-language search across 800 million verified candidate profiles.


##


**Metaview alternatives FAQ**


###


**How much does Metaview cost, and is the free plan enough?**


Metaview has per-agent pricing, meaning you pay for the functions you use, whether that’s note-taking, sourcing, or application review. Each agent has a free tier with a monthly cap, with paid plans that unlock higher usage limits.


###


**Which Metaview alternatives score candidates rather than only documenting interviews?**


Several[AI hiring tools](https://juicebox.ai/blog/best-ai-hiring-tools) score candidates and can serve as Metaview alternatives, including BrightHire, Screenloop, and Ashby. Screenloop creates detailed interview scorecards and ranks candidates. Ashby scores candidates during first-round screening inside the ATS, and BrightHire adds candidate summaries and topic coverage to support evaluation.


###


**Do general meeting notetakers work for recruiting, or do you need a recruiting-native tool?**


General meeting notetakers can work well for recruiting, usefully documenting and summarizing interviews and calls. But recruiting-native tools offer more advanced functions, like screening and candidate scoring, and are designed to integrate with your ATS. However, if you are working at lower volumes, are on a budget, or want a tool that will work across the whole business and not just recruiting functions, a general meeting notetaker may be better.
